key_insight: FlatSounds reveals that current video-to-audio (V2A) models often produce perceptually plausible soundtracks but fail to reliably reflect single-factor physical changes; a controlled counterfactual benchmark exposes these physical-reasoning gaps.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of standardized evaluations for physical correctness and causal sensitivity in V2A systems by providing targeted tests that vary one physical factor at a time to audit whether models respond appropriately.
method: Create controlled counterfactual video pairs where exactly one physical factor (e.g., material, impact force, distance, object size) is changed while everything else is held constant.
Design single-video pattern tests that probe temporal and factor-specific response patterns (e.g., amplitude, timbre, delay) to isolate model sensitivity.
Evaluate models with quantitative physical-sensitivity metrics plus complementary human/perceptual judgments to compare physical correctness vs. perceptual realism.
impact: Enables practitioners to diagnose and improve V2A models for tasks that require physically faithful audio (robotics, simulation, AR/VR) and guides development toward models with stronger causal and robustness properties.
visual_elements: Side-by-side counterfactual frame pairs annotated with the single changed factor and corresponding audio waveform/spectrogram differences
Bar chart or radar plot comparing models on 'physical-sensitivity' vs 'perceptual-realism' metrics
Timeline/spectrogram visualization showing how changing one factor (e.g., force) alters acoustic features over time
Icon grid summarizing tested physical factors (material, distance, force, size) with pass/fail badges per model
paper_authors: Tingle Li, Siddharth Gururani, Kevin J. Shih, Gantavya Bhatt, Sang-gil Lee
